newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil B Band plan faces possible delay - minister.
newsitem.headline: Brazil B Band plan faces possible delay - minister.

text.p: Brazil's plan to tender out B Band cellular concessions could be delayed by months if the country's supreme court rules against a "minimum" telecom law, Communications Minsiter Sergio Motta said.

"The power of the (Supreme Federal Tribunal) is sovereign," Motta told reporters. "If the injunction were granted it would interupt the B Band process which would only be resumed once the (General Telecommunications) Law has been passed."
Left-wing political parties are have challenged the constitutionality of the so-called minimum law and want the STF to issue an injunction halting the B Band program.

The General Telecommunications Law, a wider ranging piece of legislation, is being mulled in a committee in the Chamber of Deputies and is only likely to clear Congress at the end of June, Motta said.
The supreme court was scheduled to meet during Wednesday with the minimum law one of several items on the agenda.
The government intends to receive bids April 7 from groups interested in operating B Band services in ten regional areas of Brazil over 15 years.
Motta said he expected intense competition from consortia seeking to win the concessions, with regions covering the states of Sao Paulo, Rio de Janeiro and Minas Gerais the hottest items.
The ten concessions are worth a minimum of 3.78 billion reais but bidders are likely to pay a total of around 5.0 billion reais, the minister said.
